newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds join European relief rally after soft U.S. inflation numbers to end strong, with the positive tone seen continuing up to midweek, when further data will be watched for confirmation of bullish mood.

The Dutch long bond ended up over a point and a half, with the ten year up nearly a full point, as Bunds and Treasuries powered ahead following a rise of just 0.1 percent, half the expected increase, in the U.S. consumer price index in March.
The soft figure at least partially allayed fears that the Federal Reserve would be forced into raising U.S. interest rates again in May, dealers said.

A strong rally by Bund futures through several key resistances had cleared the outlook for the local market for the week ahead, they added, with U.S. March industrial production and capacity utilisation data on Wednesday likely to determine whether the positive sentiment persists.

The across-the-board reaction to the U.S. figures had gone some way to dispelling the heavy lull in trade afflicting the local market over the last week, one broker said, but cash flows were still not there in size.
Spreads to Germany were steady again through the session, despite some analysts tipping the Dutch market to underperform.
Some commentators have been pointing to a recent run of firm local economic indicators as a possible indication of coming yield convergence at the longer end.
Others, however, see little reason to expect significant flows into Germany in this area and are focusing attention on shorter maturities.
Along the Guilder curve, the flattening trend accelerated, with the 10-two year spread narrowing by eight basis points, to 220.
